headline: Add the paths from above and left
statement: A robot starts in the upper-left cell of an m by n grid. Each move goes one cell right or down. Count the routes to the lower-right cell; the grid has no obstacles.
constraints: The answer is guaranteed at most 2 × 10^9
intuition: A cell can be reached from the cell above it or from the cell on its left. Add those two route counts to get the count for this cell. Save the counts as you move through the grid, so different routes do not make you solve the same smaller question repeatedly.
approach: Swap the dimensions if needed so n is min(original m, original n); transposing exchanges right/down moves without changing route counts.
Initialize the first row of dp to ones: each cell has one horizontal route.
For each subsequent row, leave dp[0] as one and add dp[col - 1] into dp[col].
correctness: Induct on rows and columns. Border cells each have one route. For an interior cell, the two possible last moves partition all routes, so their counts sum to the correct count. Row-major updates preserve the required above and left values.
bruteForce: Recursively branch right and down for each move; without memoization the same cells are recomputed exponentially often.

complexity.explanation: A single row along the smaller dimension stores all needed subproblems; transposition preserves the number of paths.

pitfalls: There are no obstacles in this problem.
Initialize borders to one, not zero.
The dimensions count cells, so the route uses m+n-2 moves.
